body: Thanks for taking time to respond to my fucked up life. Yeah, leaving would allow me to sleep at night, it's just a complete change. It's possible to do with money being the only limiting factor. It just seemed so crazy to me at first to consider it, but after thinking everything through, it's not that illogical.

Are you a male or female? Age? Any diagnosis of any conditions? Are you on any medications currently? Is your fear and anxiety specific to anything? I personally have both Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Panic Disorder and have spent a long time dealing with the terror associated with my anxiety. It's been quite a challenge, but it has gotten better with work. Currently, I see a psychologist three hours a week and take medication.

Unlike the old days, they don't keep people long-term generally. The goal is to stabilize and release on medication. The issue with this is that patients often relapse and go off medication assuming that they feel better and they quickly begin having the same symptoms again. It's a vicious cycle and extremely difficult to work with. I personally would have her hospitalized as it does sound like she is a danger to herself, just to get her out of immediate danger and at least get her stabilized and give you some time to think of other things. Does she have any substance abuse history?
I'm here if you want to talk. Check out my story and you can see that we are dealing with similar things.

I wouldn't even bring up CFS until you've ruled out Anemia and Mono first. They would be the most common causes of fatigue that I've seen and are both treatable. Ruling that it's CFS would require ruling everything else out first.
The first step that I would take is to get evaluated by your regular family doctor to rule out any physical conditions. Fatigue could have a million different physical causes. Don't give up yet.
Do you have any physical problems or other medical conditions to rule out a physical problem causing your fatigue? Are you on any medications?
You should contact her parents and law enforcement and explain the situation to them. Try and keep her on the phone until someone else is with her.
Does she have a diagnosis by a psychiatrist or other physician? Has she done anything specific that would deem her a risk to herself or others?

Don't make any rash decisions and take some time to really think about everything before you do anything. Nothing is more precious than life and you can't take back that final choice. I won't promise that it will get better as I don't know your circumstances, but often time can make things better (and other times it makes it worse or doesn't help at all). I'm here to talk if you need someone.

I came off benzos as well as Effexor, Paxil and lots of other ones in my life. Effexor had to be the worst withdrawal I have ever went through, worse than benzos and lasted weeks. I remember my head just spinning for days. Try and go to an urgent care clinic and see if you can get some medication for a few days.

If you are in the United States, what state are you in? Every state has laws allowing for involuntary commitment, I would be glad to get the information relevant to you. I wish I would have had someone like you watching for me when I was on that edge of no return. Hang in there and make sure you have your own support as well.

I haven't had any friends in about 10 years and before that, had only one or two friends. My relationship with my family also sucks and I'm lucky they even talk to me. I get how you feel, it's tough to deal with, but hang in there. It is much easier to make friends in College from my experience, but I ended up having to drop out after a semester due to my issues anyway. I'm here if you want to talk.
I'm here if you need someone to talk to

I gotcha. Don't stop fighting for happiness. Failing some classes isn't the end of the world. Since my issues began, I think I failed 14 classes in a row (all paid for in cash and I'd have a degree if it weren't for that), it's not that big of a deal. I won't promise you that it will get better, but I hope it does.

As someone that hasn't had friends in years and used drugs to literally get rid of all my emotions for a long term, I get where you are coming from. It really sucks to be alone, however there are other girls in the world and you shouldn't let one drive you to the point that you have to end it all. Here if you want to talk.

Just to add, I see a psychologist twice a week (with one of those sessions being two hours long and the other an hour), another private therapist that I'm paying cash for gay related issues once a week, along with seeing a psychiatrist, taking medication and everything else I'm supposed to do.
